newsitem.title: CANADA: Martin says to keep cutting deficit.
newsitem.headline: Martin says to keep cutting deficit.

text.p: Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Tuesday he was committed to his deficit reduction policy and hinted that a tax cut may not be in his plans for the budget for fiscal 1997/98.
In a live interview with the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation, Martin said he would love to cut taxes, but that his battle with the deficit was not finished.

"I would love to be the minister of finance who brought in a tax cut," Martin said. "But Canadians can do the math every bit as well as I can and Canadians know that while we've made enormous success with deficit reduction, the battle hasn't been won... And I don't think Canadians want us to stop the job when it is only half done."

Martin is expected to deliver his final update on the fiscal year 1995/96 (April-March) sometime this fall. The update is also likely to contain some preview numbers for the current and the next fiscal year budgets.
He said a few more spending cuts were likely, but it was important to keep on track with the government's deficit reduction targets.
